dataset_version: 119th Congress public laws 1-80, GPO USLM 2.0.17 conversion, as published on govinfo
schema: USLM 2.0.17 (https://www.govinfo.gov/schemas/xml/uslm/uslm-2.0.17.xsd), maintained by the U.S. Government Publishing Office (https://github.com/usgpo/uslm)
license: Public domain. Each file carries <dc:rights>Pursuant to Title 17 Section 105 of the United States Code, this file is not subject to copyright protection and is in the public domain.</dc:rights>
attribution_required: None legally required. Recommended: U.S. Government Publishing Office, govinfo, PLAW collection, USLM XML.
sha256_of_archive_note: No upstream archive exists for this slice; files were fetched individually. This value is the manifest digest = sha256 over the sorted lines "<file sha256>  xml/<file name>\n" for the 79 XML files under xml/ (provenance.json and files_manifest.tsv are excluded from the digest). Per-file digests are in files_manifest.tsv.
selection_rule: Deterministic: for N = 1..80 in ascending order, fetch https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/PLAW-119publ{N}/uslm/PLAW-119publ{N}.xml; discard any single file larger than 8,000,000 bytes; stop once the retained total reaches 30,000,000 bytes. Result: 79 files retained, 9,959,471 bytes total.
stability_note: GPO re-runs its USLM converter over time (each file records <processedBy> and <processedDate>). These bytes are pinned by sha256 as fetched on the accessed_utc above; a later re-fetch may differ and MUST be treated as a new dataset_version.

what_ground_truth.a_typed_anchor_extraction: STRONG for STATUTORY CITATIONS, weak for money/date/duration. 5,105 <ref href="..."> elements give the surface citation string AND its resolved canonical target, e.g. <ref href="/us/usc/t8/s1226/c">8 U.S.C. 1226(c)</ref> -> title 8, section 1226, subsection (c). 3,455 target the U.S. Code and 122 target the CFR. That is span + typed normalized value, which is exactly the shape an anchor extractor should be scored on. Dates: only 79 <date date="YYYY-MM-DD"> elements (essentially the approval date of each law), so this is NOT a date-anchor corpus. Money amounts, percentages, and durations appear in the text but are NOT tagged.
what_ground_truth.b_structural_parsing: STRONG / primary. 15,199 nested hierarchy elements (section > subsection > paragraph > subparagraph > clause > subclause > item), each with a sibling <num value="a">(a) </num> element carrying both the rendered enumerator and its normalized value, and 8,870 of them additionally carrying a canonical @identifier path such as /us/pl/119/1/s2/1/E/i. Headings are separately tagged (<heading>), and lead-in text is tagged <chapeau>, so heading-vs-body and lead-in-vs-item are decidable, not guessed. 555 <term> elements mark defined terms at their point of definition, which is partial gold for a defined-term index.
what_ground_truth.c_tracked_changes_markup: CLOSEST PUBLIC PROXY, but NOT redline gold. 4,349 <amendingAction type="amend|insert|delete|redesignate|add|..."> elements paired with 2,566 <quotedText> and 647 <quotedContent> elements encode typed edit operations against a target document with the exact struck/inserted text. That validates 'produce a typed, addressed edit operation with exact text', which is the semantic core of a redline. It does NOT validate OOXML w:ins/w:del/w:comment emission, revision-mark round-tripping, or Word compatibility.

why_this_corpus: Independent of every contract-review benchmark family (CUAD/MAUD/ContractNLI/LegalBench/LegalBench-RAG and Harvey LAB), so a structure parser scored here cannot be scoring its own training distribution. It is also editorially produced rather than crowd-annotated, so the hierarchy and citation targets are publisher ground truth, not a heuristic projection.
